items.title: 67520_George Handy oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee discusses Barbara Cade only in the context of her displacing another singer (Barbara Cox/Ginnie) from a job in Boyd Raeburn's band. The interviewee states 'I did mind' regarding her singing, but there is no evidence of a direct personal relationship, collaboration, or meeting between

ctx.x: Bad reasons; for personal reasons. She didn't like so and so and that was it, she wanted Boyd to get rid of a guy because she didn't like him, and Boyd did it. She knocked a kid out of a job to get the job for herself, before she married Boyd; they were going together and she was singing with Jerry Wald, with the Jerry Wald Orchestra and she left the band to come out to California to live with Boyd. She would come on the bandstand and they would come over to me and ask me if I minded if she would sing, and I did…
Who was the singer at that time, Barbara Cade?

Barbara Cox, I think. The girl that David married. She knocked Barbara out of the job and Boyd hired Ginnie. Ginnie was a better singer than Barbara; in terms of singing he made an improvement. I can't argue against that, what I didn't like was the way it was done.
